newsitem.title: USA: Ranariddh said to disavow Khmer Rouge.
newsitem.headline: Ranariddh said to disavow Khmer Rouge.

text.p: Cambodia's Prince Norodom Ranariddh promised the United States on Friday he would not bring the Khmer Rouge guerrilla group into government if he is restored to power in Phnom Penh, the State Department said.
During a meeting with Undersecretary of State Thomas Pickering, Ranariddh said: "I have nothing to do with the Khmer Rouge and I will not bring them into positions of power," the department said.

The department spokesman, Nicholas Burns, told reporters: "Needless to say, that is a welcome commitment by Prince Ranariddh because we firmly oppose any participation by the Khmer Rouge in Cambodian politics."
Asked if the United States believed Ranariddh's pledge, Burns replied: "What means more than words is deeds."

What the State Department calls Ranariddh's "flirtation" with the Khmer Rouge has been a problem for Washington as it seeks to support diplomatic efforts to end the crisis in Cambodia, in which Ranariddh, First Prime Minister in a coalition government, was ousted last weekend by forces loyal to his co-premier, Hun Sen.
The Khmer Rouge were responsible for the deaths of more than one million people when the group ruled Cambodia from 1975 to 1979.
